verses.text: 269. The Holy Scriptures repeatedly confess the universal power of God. He is called the “Mighty One of Jacob,” the “Lord of hosts,” the “strong and mighty” one. If God is almighty “in heaven and on earth,” it is because he made them. (Gen 49:24; Isa 1:24 etc.; Ps 24:8–10; 135:6.) Nothing is impossible with God, who disposes his works according to his will. (Cf. Jer 27:5; 32:17; Lk 1:37.) He is the Lord of the universe, whose order he established and which remains wholly subject to him and at his disposal. He is master of history, governing hearts and events in keeping with his will: “It is always in your power to show great strength, and who can withstand the strength of your arm?” (Wis 11:21; cf. Esth 4:17b; Prov 21:1; Tob 13:2.)
